hook: A bus fare app shows two lines: one climbing steeply, one barely tilting. Both "go up", but one says fares jump fast with distance and the other says they hardly change. The tilt of a line, its slope, is the number that tells them apart, and the shape of every economics curve is a statement about how two variables move.

prereq.q: On a graph, the ordered pair (20, 7) means
options: 20 across on the horizontal axis and 7 up the vertical axis
20 up the vertical axis and 7 across
a change of 20 followed by a change of 7
prereq.why: The horizontal value comes first, then the vertical value.

prereq.q: Two variables rise together. Their relationship is
prereq.why: A direct relationship means both rise or fall together.

figure.caption: Four shapes: upward sloping (positive slope), downward sloping (negative slope), a vertical line and a horizontal line.

chain.cause: You pick two points on a line
chain.effect: you can find the rise (change in the vertical value) and the run (change in the horizontal value)

chain.cause: You divide the rise by the run
chain.effect: you get the slope, positive if the line rises and negative if it falls

chain.cause: A line is vertical or horizontal
chain.effect: one variable stays fixed while the other changes
its slope changes along it, getting steeper as it falls

ideas: Slope = rise over run = change in the vertical value divided by the change in the horizontal value.
Upward sloping: positive slope, a direct relationship. Downward sloping: negative slope, an inverse relationship.
A vertical line keeps the horizontal value fixed; a horizontal line keeps the vertical value fixed and has a slope of zero.
A straight line has one slope everywhere; a bowed curve does not.

misconception.wrong: Slope is run over rise: how far across for each step up.
misconception.right: Slope is rise over run: the change in the vertical value divided by the change in the horizontal value. Flipping them gives the reciprocal, a different number.

summary: Slope is rise over run, the change in the vertical value divided by the change in the horizontal value. A line that rises to the right has a positive slope, one that falls has a negative slope, a horizontal line has a slope of zero, and a vertical line keeps the horizontal value fixed. A straight line has the same slope at every point, while a bowed curve changes slope as you move along it.
